prerequisites: Install Instrilo v0.2.3 or newer from a release. Check instrilo --version, then prepare the tutorial workspace as shown below.
Use Bash on macOS/Linux or WSL, inside your prepared tutorial workspace. Keep every step in the same terminal.
Use a fresh tutorial project name. If init/create says the project already exists, choose a new slug and update INSTRILO_PROJECT; do not delete work you want to keep.

next.label: Inspect the tutorial fixtures and checks

title: Build an agent that looks up an order
summary: See a model request a real HTTP tool, receive its result, and produce a grounded answer.
outcome: A generated agent executes an actual read-only HTTP request and records its model → tool → model trace.

verification.scope: The generated native TypeScript runtime calls the deterministic model endpoint twice and the synthetic order lookup once, enforcing the tool input schema. The bundled verify.mjs helper only reads saved JSON and asserts the expected results.
limitations: The deterministic fixture checks integration behavior, not model intelligence or response quality.
No paid model account, real credentials or cloud resource is used. Package installation still needs registry access.
The model decision is scripted. The endpoint contains synthetic public data and no authentication; do not copy that access policy to private customer systems.
This walkthrough verifies a read-only tool. It does not establish approval, tenant isolation or safe write semantics.

steps.title: Create an order-support project
steps.body: Start with the native runtime and add only the explicit connection and tool needed for this task.
steps.expected: An isolated local project is created.

steps.title: Start the named local demonstration service
steps.body: This bundled helper runs on an available localhost port. It returns deterministic model replies and synthetic order data. It is a demonstration service, not a real LLM. The EXIT trap stops only its tracked process if a later command fails.
steps.code:
node examples/quickstarts/foundations/fixture.mjs serve "$INSTRILO_PROJECT/fixture.json" > "$INSTRILO_PROJECT/fixture.log" 2>&1 &
INSTRILO_FIXTURE_PID=$!
trap 'kill "$INSTRILO_FIXTURE_PID" 2>/dev/null || true' EXIT
node examples/quickstarts/foundations/fixture.mjs wait "$INSTRILO_PROJECT/fixture.json"
node examples/quickstarts/foundations/fixture.mjs files "$INSTRILO_PROJECT/fixture.json" "$INSTRILO_PROJECT/connections"
export INSTRILO_TUTORIAL_BEARER=tutorial-bearer
steps.expected: The helper prints “Local deterministic fixture is ready” and writes five JSON connection/tool documents containing its actual local port.

steps.title: Connect the model route and the lookup tool
steps.body: The HTTP endpoint contains one synthetic order. The tool is read-only, has no required scopes and needs no approval in this local example. Real private data needs endpoint authentication and authorization appropriate to its users.
steps.code:
instrilo connections add answering "$INSTRILO_PROJECT" --file "$INSTRILO_PROJECT/connections/tool-runtime.json"
instrilo connections use runtime answering "$INSTRILO_PROJECT"
instrilo tools add "$INSTRILO_PROJECT" --file "$INSTRILO_PROJECT/connections/lookup-tool.json"
instrilo tools list "$INSTRILO_PROJECT"
instrilo validate "$INSTRILO_PROJECT"
steps.expected: lookup_order is configured as a GET tool with a strict orderId schema. Project validation reports valid: true.

steps.title: Generate, prepare and ask about the order
steps.body: The fixture model returns a tool call, not the final order status. The generated runtime must perform the HTTP lookup and send the returned result back before an answer is produced.
steps.code:
instrilo build "$INSTRILO_PROJECT"
instrilo prepare "$INSTRILO_PROJECT"
instrilo run "$INSTRILO_PROJECT" --input 'Where is order ORD-1042?' > "$INSTRILO_PROJECT/run.json"
cat "$INSTRILO_PROJECT/run.json"
node examples/quickstarts/foundations/verify.mjs native-tool "$INSTRILO_PROJECT"
steps.expected: The answer includes “shipped” and “LOCAL-123”. The trace is exactly model, tool, model.

steps.title: Verify that a real tool request occurred
steps.body: Service counters prevent a canned final response from passing the walkthrough without an actual lookup.
steps.expected: Exactly two model requests and one order lookup are observed.

steps.title: Stop the fixture you started
steps.body: Keep the generated project and evidence. Stop only this tutorial process; no broad process matching or machine cleanup is needed.
steps.code:
kill "$INSTRILO_FIXTURE_PID"
wait "$INSTRILO_FIXTURE_PID" || true
trap - EXIT
printf 'Tutorial fixture stopped. Project files are retained.
'
steps.expected: The fixture stops and project files remain in .studio/tutorials.

troubleshooting: If preparation cannot reach npm/PyPI, fix registry/proxy access and repeat prepare; it does not require model credentials.
If the project already exists, inspect or keep it and choose a new tutorial slug. Do not rerun init over an existing manifest.
If schema validation fails, keep the case-sensitive orderId field and the documented synthetic value ORD-1042. Read the generated tool definition before changing it.
cleanup: The final step stops the tracked fixture process. Generated code and run.json are retained.
